title: STEPP – Structured outpatient teletherapy occupational therapy and physiotherapy for Parkinson’s disease
summary:
To answer the research questions, various methods are combined. This approach takes into account both the experiences and assessments of professionals as well as measurable outcomes and feedback from patients. The different methods complement one another, thereby enabling a comprehensive examination of the topic.
For the qualitative component, interviews are conducted with experts. While prepared questions are used, respondents are also given the opportunity to discuss their experiences and specific situations from the practice of teletherapy in detail.
For the quantitative component, various questionnaires and standardized procedures are employed. These are used to assess, among other things, treatment success, patient satisfaction, and other aspects relevant to the project. In addition, a custom questionnaire is being developed. This questionnaire takes into account the results of previous research, the interviews with experts, the questionnaires and procedures used, and the project’s research questions.
Combining this diverse information creates a comprehensive picture of teletherapy. The results are then jointly evaluated and presented in an accessible manner.

interventions.name:
An observational study to determine the extent to which a combination of in-person and teletherapy within outpatient occupational and physical therapy care can improve therapeutic outcomes and satisfaction among people with Parkinson’s disease, as well as their caregivers and family members.

Cooperation agreements will be established with outpatient occupational therapists and physical therapists to recruit participants. This collaboration will continue throughout the entire recruitment period.

Once consent has been obtained, the family members of the study participants will also be surveyed at the beginning and end of their participation in the study via questionnaires, interviews, and assessments regarding their subjective experiences and evaluations of the study’s effects.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Be of legal age (≥ 18 years),
•    Have given informed consent to participate in the study,
•    Have sufficient knowledge of German to be able to understand and answer the information and questions required for the respective survey,
•    For therapists: professional registration as an occupational therapist or physiotherapist
•    For patients: medically diagnosed Parkinson’s disease
Exclusion criteria:
•    lack of or withdrawal of consent to participate in the study,
•    insufficient knowledge of German to enable meaningful participation in the relevant survey,
•    for therapists: lack of professional registration as an occupational therapist or physiotherapist
•    for patients: no medically diagnosed Parkinson’s disease and/or medical diagnoses that result in cognitive, communicative or other functional limitations and which prevent independent and meaningful participation in the relevant data collection
